articles.title: SDFoam: Signed-Distance Foam for explicit surface reconstruction
articles.authors: Antonella Rech, Nicola Conci, and Nicola Garau
articles.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
articles.summary: SDFoam is a surface reconstruction method that combines signed distance fields with a foam-based explicit representation. It aims to recover cleaner, more coherent surfaces by deriving density from an SDF while preserving the controllability and mesh extraction advantages of Voronoi-style cells.

articles.title: VolHuMe: a High-Resolution Large Scale Dataset of Volumetric Human Meshes
articles.authors: Giulia Martinelli, Niccolò Bisagno, Nicola Garau, Esa Rahtu, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
articles.summary: VolHuMe is a high-resolution large-scale dataset of volumetric human meshes captured with a professional close-range volumetric studio. VolHuMe provides 104 subjects and 156K annotated frames with rich supervision for 4D human reconstruction, rendering, and avatar research.

articles.title: Tackling Cross-Lingual Generalization in Speech Emotion Recognition via Linguistic Grouping: A Spotlight on Neo-Latin Languages
articles.authors: Francesco Ardan Dal Rì, Nicola Garau, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: EUSIPCO 2026

articles.title: Render, Encode, Plan: A simple pipeline for hybrid RL-DL learning inside Unreal Engine
articles.authors: Daniele Della Pietra and Nicola Garau
articles.venue: Computers & Graphics
articles.summary: Render, Encode, Plan is a hybrid reinforcement-learning and deep-learning pipeline built inside Unreal Engine. It renders visual observations, encodes them into compact representations, and uses them for planning, making simulated visual learning easier to prototype and evaluate.

articles.title: Build-A-Volcap: Automated Synthetic Validation of Real-World Volumetric Capture Quality
articles.authors: Antonella Rech, Giulia Martinelli, Nicola Garau, Nicola Conci, and Francesco De Natale
articles.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing Workshops (ICIPW)
articles.summary: Build-A-Volcap is a synthetic validation framework for predicting the quality of real-world volumetric capture setups. It simulates capture configurations and evaluates reconstruction quality automatically, helping designers assess camera layouts before deploying physical systems.

articles.title: Drone Agents: learning to fly to learn how to see
articles.authors: Daniele Della Pietra, Karthik Govindarajan, Fabrizio Granelli, Andrea Rosani, and Nicola Garau
articles.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Visual and Signal-Based Systems (AVSS)
articles.summary: Drone Agents explores embodied visual learning with UAVs, where a drone learns flight behavior that improves what it can observe. The method links navigation and perception, using simulated drone agents to gather better visual evidence for downstream understanding tasks.

articles.title: To Infinity and Beyond: a GPU-driven memory sharing pipeline to generate and process infinite synthetic data
articles.authors: Daniele Della Pietra, Gino Lanzo Hahn, and Nicola Garau
articles.venue: Proceedings of the Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Posters
articles.summary: To Infinity and Beyond presents a GPU-driven memory sharing pipeline for streaming synthetic data directly from a graphics engine to learning code. By avoiding disk-based dataset generation, it enables real-time training or processing over virtually unlimited synthetic scenes.

articles.title: CLaP-Contrast Label Predict: a quest for cheaper labeling in 3D human pose estimation
articles.authors: Davide Cavicchini, Alessia Pivotto, Sofia Lorengo, Andrea Rosani, and Nicola Garau
articles.venue: Proceedings of the Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
articles.summary: CLaP is a label-efficient framework for 3D human pose estimation that reduces dependence on expensive 3D annotations. It combines contrastive learning with label prediction to exploit cheaper supervision while preserving useful pose representations.

articles.title: MoMa: Skinned motion retargeting using masked pose modeling
articles.authors: Giulia Martinelli, Nicola Garau, Niccolò Bisagno, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Computer Vision and Image Understanding
articles.summary: MoMa is a motion retargeting method based on masked pose modeling. It learns to transfer skinned motion across characters and skeletons by reconstructing missing or corrupted pose information, improving robustness to different body structures.

articles.title: Agglomerator++: Interpretable part-whole hierarchies and latent space representations in neural networks
articles.authors: Zeno Sambugaro, Nicola Garau, Niccolò Bisagno, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Computer Vision and Image Understanding
articles.summary: Agglomerator++ studies interpretability in neural networks by building part-whole hierarchies from learned representations. It extends the Agglomerator idea to expose relationships between low-level parts, higher-level concepts, and latent-space structure.

articles.title: All skeletons are created equal! a domain adaptation transformer to handle multiple topologies
articles.authors: Giulia Martinelli, Nicola Garau, Niccolo Bisagno, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
articles.summary: This paper introduces a domain adaptation transformer for human pose data with different skeleton topologies. It maps heterogeneous joint layouts into a common representation, allowing pose models to transfer more easily across datasets and annotation formats.

articles.title: Unicrowd simulator: Visual and behavioral fidelity for the generation of crowd datasets
articles.authors: Niccolò Bisagno, Antonio Luigi Stefani, Nicola Garau, Francesco De Natale, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
articles.summary: UniCrowd is a simulation framework for generating crowd datasets with both visual realism and plausible behavior. It combines controllable virtual environments with crowd motion modeling to support training and evaluation of crowd analysis methods.

articles.title: Dynamic crowd routing: Rl-driven crowd dynamics
articles.authors: Daniele Della Pietra, Nicola Garau, Nicola Conci, and Fabrizio Granelli
articles.venue: 2024 IEEE 26th International Workshop on Multimedia Signal Processing (MMSP)
articles.summary: Dynamic Crowd Routing uses reinforcement learning to control and adapt crowd motion in simulated environments. The framework learns routing policies that influence collective pedestrian dynamics, enabling more flexible and responsive crowd simulations.

articles.title: Skeleton-aware motion retargeting using masked pose modeling
articles.authors: Giulia Martinelli, Nicola Garau, Niccolò Bisagno, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: European Conference on Computer Vision
articles.summary: This work proposes skeleton-aware motion retargeting through masked pose modeling. It learns motion transfer between different skeletons by masking and reconstructing pose sequences, encouraging the model to capture motion semantics rather than relying on a fixed topology.

articles.title: Epoch: Jointly estimating the 3d pose of cameras and humans
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Giulia Martinelli, Niccolò Bisagno, Denis Tomè, and Carsten Stoll
articles.venue: European Conference on Computer Vision
articles.summary: EPOCH is a framework for monocular 3D human pose estimation that uses the full perspective camera model instead of common weak-perspective approximations. It jointly estimates camera parameters and 3D pose through a lifter network and a regressor network, establishing an unambiguous 2D-to-3D relationship.

articles.title: Peek-a-bot: learning through vision in unreal engine
articles.authors: Daniele Della Pietra, Nicola Garau, Nicola Conci, and Fabrizio Granelli
articles.venue: The Eurographics Association

articles.summary: Peek-a-bot is an Unreal Engine framework for visual learning with an embodied agent. It lets an agent actively observe a scene and learn from rendered visual feedback, supporting experiments that connect perception, action, and simulation.

articles.title: A Unified Simulation Framework for Visual and Behavioral Fidelity in Crowd Analysis
articles.authors: Niccolò Bisagno, Nicola Garau, Antonio Luigi Stefani, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2312.02613
articles.summary: This work presents a unified crowd simulation framework that targets both visual fidelity and behavioral realism. It is designed to generate synthetic crowd data with realistic appearance, motion, and interaction patterns for crowd analysis research.

articles.title: CapsulePose: A variational CapsNet for real-time end-to-end 3D human pose estimation
articles.authors: Nicola Garau and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Neurocomputing
articles.summary: CapsulePose is a real-time end-to-end 3D human pose estimation method based on variational capsule networks. It exploits capsule representations to model pose structure and viewpoint-related transformations directly from visual input.

articles.title: Capsules as viewpoint learners for human pose estimation
articles.authors: Nicola Garau and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2302.06194
articles.summary: This paper investigates capsule networks as viewpoint-aware learners for human pose estimation. It studies how capsule representations can encode transformations and help pose models reason about body configuration under changing camera viewpoints.

articles.title: A multimodal framework for the evaluation of patients’ weaknesses, supporting the design of customised AAL solutions
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Damiano Fruet, Alessandro Luchetti, Francesco De Natale, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Expert Systems with Applications
articles.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal assessment framework for evaluating patient weaknesses in Ambient Assisted Living scenarios. It combines different sensing and analysis modalities to support the design of personalized assistive solutions.

articles.title: Networked Musical XR: where’s the limit? A preliminary investigation on the joint use of point clouds and low-latency audio communication
articles.authors: Luca Turchet, Nicola Garau, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Audio Mostly Conference
articles.summary: Networked Musical XR studies the feasibility of shared extended-reality music performance using point clouds and low-latency audio. It investigates the practical limits of combining volumetric visual presence with time-sensitive musical communication.

articles.title: Design of Viewpoint-Equivariant Networks to Improve Human Pose Estimation
articles.authors: Nicola Garau
articles.venue: Università degli studi di Trento
articles.summary: This thesis investigates viewpoint-equivariant neural architectures for improving human pose estimation. It focuses on models that explicitly reason about camera viewpoint changes, especially through capsule-based and geometry-aware representations.

articles.title: Gender recognition from 3D shape parameters
articles.authors: Giulia Martinelli, Nicola Garau, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: International Conference on Image Analysis and Processing
articles.summary: This paper studies gender recognition using 3D body shape parameters rather than images alone. It analyzes how compact parametric body representations can support classification while abstracting away pose, texture, and acquisition conditions.

articles.title: Interpretable part-whole hierarchies and conceptual-semantic relationships in neural networks
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Niccolò Bisagno, Zeno Sambugaro, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference on computer vision and pattern recognition
articles.summary: This paper introduces a method for extracting interpretable part-whole hierarchies from neural networks. It reveals how learned features compose into semantic concepts, making internal representations more understandable for visual recognition models.

articles.title: DECA: Deep viewpoint-Equivariant human pose estimation using Capsule Autoencoders
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Niccolo Bisagno, Piotr Bròdka, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
articles.summary: DECA is a viewpoint-equivariant approach to human pose estimation based on capsule autoencoders. It learns representations that disentangle pose content from viewpoint transformations, improving generalization across camera views.

articles.title: Panoptop: a framework for generating viewpoint-invariant human pose estimation datasets
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Giulia Martinelli, Piotr Bròdka, Niccolo Bisagno, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
articles.summary: PanopTOP is a framework for generating human pose datasets with systematic viewpoint variation. It supports viewpoint-invariant pose estimation research by creating controlled multi-view training data from human motion and camera transformations.

articles.title: Fast automatic camera network calibration through human mesh recovery
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Francesco G. B. De Natale, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Journal of Real-Time Image Processing
articles.summary: This paper proposes a fast automatic calibration method for camera networks using recovered human meshes. By aligning human shape and pose evidence across views, it estimates camera geometry with minimal manual intervention.

articles.title: Unsupervised continuous camera network pose estimation through human mesh recovery
articles.authors: Nicola Garau and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on Distributed Smart Cameras
articles.summary: This work addresses unsupervised, continuous pose estimation for camera networks using human mesh recovery. It uses people moving through the scene as calibration cues, enabling camera pose refinement without dedicated calibration targets.

articles.title: Virtual crowds: An LSTM-based framework for crowd simulation
articles.authors: Niccolò Bisagno, Nicola Garau, Andrea Montagner, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: International Conference on Image Analysis and Processing
articles.summary: Virtual Crowds is an LSTM-based framework for simulating pedestrian trajectories. It learns motion patterns from data and generates plausible crowd behavior, supporting synthetic crowd analysis and virtual environment applications.

articles.title: Technological infrastructure supports new paradigm of care for healthy aging: The living lab Ausilia
articles.authors: Andrea Grisenti, Giandomenico Nollo, Michela Dalprá, Francesco De Natale, Mariolino De Cecco, Andrea Francesconi, Alberto Fornaser, Paolo Tomasin, Nicola Garau, Luca Guandalini, and et al.
articles.venue: Italian Forum of Ambient Assisted Living
articles.summary: This paper describes the Ausilia living lab as a technological infrastructure for healthy aging and assistive care. It presents an environment where sensing, monitoring, and user-centered technologies can be tested for new care models.

articles.title: Joint trajectory and fatigue analysis in wheelchair users
articles.authors: Maddalena Sebastiani, Nicola Garau, Francesco De Natale, and Nicola Conci
articles.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops
articles.summary: This paper analyzes wheelchair-user trajectories together with fatigue-related information. It aims to connect movement behavior and physical effort, supporting better assessment of mobility, accessibility, and user condition.

articles.title: Enhancing character posing by a sketch-based interaction
articles.authors: Simone Barbieri, Nicola Garau, Wenyu Hu, Zhidong Xiao, and Xiaosong Yang
articles.venue: ACM SIGGRAPH 2016 Posters
articles.summary: This paper presents a sketch-based interface for character posing. It allows users to control or refine character poses through simple drawn input, making 3D posing more intuitive and accessible.

articles.title: Designing Modular and Multi-Modal Urban-Scale Digital Twins
articles.authors: Nicola Garau, Daniele Della Pietra, Nicola Conci, and Fabrizio Granelli
articles.venue: Available at SSRN 5212681
articles.summary: This work discusses the design of modular, multi-modal digital twins at urban scale. It focuses on integrating heterogeneous data, simulation components, and sensing modalities into a flexible architecture for city-scale analysis and decision support.
